scope: One dependency-free body-free decision boundary for evidence-backed component replace, retain, or defer recommendations; no component replacement is executed.

criteria.expected: Every suite identifies exact baseline and optional candidate component kind, id, version, and configuration hash without accepting prompts, labels, endpoints, credentials, or case bodies.
The target policy has a stable identity and establishment time that precedes every observation; targets cannot be selected after results are known.
A closed metric catalog fixes direction and unit for structural coverage, correction density, forecast readiness/assessment/calibration, human usefulness/learning, latency, tokens, and monetary cost.
Every target declares threshold, minimum paired improvement, allowed regression, required scopes, and minimum paired scenarios with range validation.
Observations remain paired by opaque scenario and scope; duplicate metrics, duplicate scenarios, mismatched units, and unpaired candidate data fail closed.
Missing observations remain not-observed, and contextual usefulness, profile-revision usefulness, and user learning count only when attributed to the user.
Each target reports scope/sample denominators, baseline and candidate means when observed, target/improvement/regression checks, limitations, and blockers.
Replacement is recommended only when every required target passes; complete failed evidence retains the baseline and incomplete evidence defers replacement.
The same normalized suite produces a deterministic identity and report without canonical, possibility, provider, package, or runtime-database writes.
P7 records the current evidence-backed retain/defer outcome and open human/real-use gaps without claiming a live-provider benchmark, executed replacement, usefulness, or human acceptance.
P0-P6 contracts, Web primacy, thin clients, data authority, provider neutrality, public/private isolation, and supply-chain/browser gates remain unchanged.
